_comment: Hand-checked extra requirements, merged into programs by src/lib/data.js (the scraper never touches this file). A program can match several entries; their items, notes and dates are combined. item.kind: form | video | interview | portfolio | audition | test | reference. Only add facts read on the official page in `sources`, and update `checked` when you re-read it. A source url of "@program" means the program's own official page.

items.label: Engineering Supplemental Application
items.detail: Mandatory: without it your application isn't considered. You list your activities since Grade 9 and your extracurriculars, and can add an optional personal statement.

items.label: Personal Profile: 3 timed video responses
items.detail: Recorded answers inside the supplemental application. They look at your reasoning and communication; there is no "right" answer.

items.label: A contact for each activity
items.detail: No reference letters, but each extracurricular needs someone (not family) who can confirm it if asked.

notes: There is no interview — the video responses are recorded, not live.
Finishing after January 15 means you aren't considered until the May round.

dates.label: Engineering: apply on OUAC for early consideration

items.label: Admission Information Form (AIF)
items.detail: Required for admission to every Engineering program.

items.label: Online video interview
items.detail: Required for all Engineering applicants. It's done online, not in person.

notes: Waterloo doesn't review AIFs submitted after the deadline.

items.label: Supplementary Information Form
items.detail: An extra form only Software Engineering applicants fill in, on top of the AIF.

items.label: Admission Information Form (AIF)

The Euclid and CSMC math contests are not required for admission, but some Faculty of Mathematics scholarships need one of them.

items.label: Portfolio (if invited)
items.detail: Selected applicants are invited to send a portfolio of creative work. Architecture doesn't use the AIF.

items.label: Casper test
items.detail: Required for all OUAC applicants. An online, open-response situational judgment test (90–110 minutes) run by Acuity Insights, taken on a computer with a webcam and microphone. You can only take it once per admissions cycle.

items.label: Register on takecasper.com
items.detail: Pick Canada, the 2026–2027 cycle and Casper 1 (CSP-10200), select Engineering, and send results to Western (UWO), Faculty of Engineering. Your name, birth date and email must match your OUAC application exactly.

notes: Test dates are only on takecasper.com, and Western says no extra dates are likely to be added — book early.
Results reach Western about 3 weeks after the test, and no offer is made until they arrive. Offers can start in November.
Register at least 3 days before your test date.

items.label: Audition (includes an interview)
items.detail: Past auditions had two contrasting monologues, one song and an interview, plus an audition questionnaire. Full 2027 details come out in November 2026. $50 fee when you book.

notes: You first get an offer to Humanities; it changes to Theatre & Drama Studies if your audition is successful. If not, your Humanities offer stays.

items.label: Audition, interview and skills assessment
items.detail: In person if you live within 300 km of Toronto; by recording (with an online interview) if you live further away. 2–3 faculty members on the panel; no theory test.

notes: Jazz programs: send a pre-screening video with the Music Questionnaire; selected applicants are invited to audition.

items.label: Statement of Interest
items.detail: Required online statement, including the name and contact information of one referee. Applicants who don’t complete it are disqualified.

items.label: One Idea supplementary application
items.detail: Make an object, document it with exactly three photographs, and write a summary (max 200 words) of the object and your key decisions. No other portfolio is accepted.

notes: You can submit only once, and the submission is final. Missing the deadline means automatic refusal.
Generative AI for images or text isn’t allowed and leads to automatic refusal.

items.label: One Idea supplementary application
items.detail: Submit six to eight images of your work and a 250–650 word statement about two or three of them.

notes: You can submit only once, and the submission is final. Missing the deadline means automatic refusal.
Generative AI for images or text isn’t allowed and leads to automatic refusal.

items.label: Supplementary Application Form (SAF)
items.detail: About your life, interests and goals. The Management prompt: “Everyone has a purpose. Everyone has a story. What’s yours?”

notes: The SAF is in the Join U of T applicant portal. Only you may write it — generative AI tools such as ChatGPT are not allowed — and you can’t change it once submitted.
If your program requires the SAF and you don’t submit it, you aren’t eligible for the program.
Management & International Business (co-op) also requires an interview.
